findings.title: L2: an unexpected exception is answered 503, but Starlette re-raises it and uvicorn logs its full text, so PostgreSQL's DETAIL row (email, names, phone) reaches the edge-bff log, against main.py's own rule
findings.root_cause: main.py:331-334 registers @app.exception_handler(Exception) with the comment 'Deliberately no exception body/traceback: database/http errors may contain secrets'. That handler lives in Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware. After the handler answers, the middleware re-raises ('We always continue to raise the exception', starlette 0.47.3 middleware/errors.py). uvicorn's protocol then logs 'Exception in ASGI application' with exc_info on logger uvicorn.error. The Dockerfile CMD (line 97) turns off only the access log, so the line goes to stderr and the Railway log. psycopg's str(exc) carries the server's DETAIL ('Failing row contains (...)', 'Key (email)=(...) already exists'; probe on my cluster). The loops keep that text out: worker.py:55-57 logs 'queue_operation_failed' only, and backtest.py:268-288 failure_of logs class and SQLSTATE. The request path has no such redaction.
findings.evidence: tests/test_r2_life.py::test_l2_an_unexpected_database_error_never_writes_the_persons_data_to_the_server_log (c9b5e53c). Under a real uvicorn server, a registration meets a database constraint the running code does not know. The person gets 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, and uvicorn.error captured 'Exception in ASGI application' plus the traceback ending 'psycopg.errors.CheckViolation ... DETAIL: Failing row contains (4, u_a75129..., null, sinta.probe@example.com, null, Sinta, Probe, +6281299990000, user, pending, ..., leak_probe, <registration_hash>)'. Same failure on a p3c-int extract (main.py:340-343 unchanged there).
findings.failure_scenario: Any write path meets an error the code does not expect. The planned beta/live split makes this routine: a migration applied for the beta adds or tightens a constraint while the live version still writes the old shape. Other cases: a Phase 4 admin edit hitting users_email_one_account, or a Phase 5 duplicate payment event (UNIQUE provider, provider_event_id) or a CHECK on its raw payload. Each time, the person's email, names, phone, the registration hash or the payment payload is written to the Railway log, outside the database's grants and retention. Anyone with project log access can read it.
findings.general_class: Framework-level logging of unhandled exceptions bypasses an application's redaction rule. The same holds for terminal-api, which has no Exception handler at all (main.py:200-210 maps only HTTPException and validation errors), so 3c's owner-row and access_log writes would log owner keys and versions. It also holds for every later route whose database write is not wrapped: Phase 4 admin forms with email and phone, Phase 5 payment webhooks with raw payloads.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c's edge-bff paths raise Refusal, which is handled without a log. terminal-api's new writes carry owner keys and entitlements versions only, not personal data.
findings.affects_beta_live: Worse: version skew between the beta's migrations and the live code turns 'unexpected' constraint errors into a normal event (the test's scenario). Each one logs the failing row.
findings.fix: Catch Exception in an outermost pure-ASGI middleware, or replace ServerErrorMiddleware's behaviour. Log only failure_of(e) (class and SQLSTATE, the loops' rule) and answer 503 without re-raising. A logging filter on uvicorn.error that drops exc_info is the minimal alternative. Apply the same to terminal-api before 3c's per-owner writes. Keep the probe test.
findings.confirm_check: cd apps/edge-bff && EDGE_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=... pytest tests/test_r2_life.py::test_l2_an_unexpected_database_error_never_writes_the_persons_data_to_the_server_log

findings.title: L3: two websites on one database share rows that per-service settings key (EDGE_MFA_KEY, EDGE_CODE_SECRET, EDGE_SESSION_SECRET, EDGE_EMAIL_MODE), and the log-mode guard trusts EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, where production will run; EXEC's beta/live consequences list names none of these
findings.root_cause: The design keeps secrets out of the database by keying stored rows with per-service settings. EDGE_MFA_KEY: the TOTP secret is HMAC(EDGE_MFA_KEY, user_id||nonce) (mfa.py:203-204), and recovery codes are HMAC'd with it (mfa.py:240-243), with one mfa_totp row per user (PK user_id, 20261116_003:143); enrolment replaces the nonce (auth_flows.py:319-320). EDGE_CODE_SECRET: code_hash uses it (auth_flows.py:126-128), with one live code per (user, purpose) and a new one consuming the old (auth_flows.py:151-152). EDGE_SESSION_SECRET: the throttle key hashes use it (main.py:226, throttle.py:64-66), and so do CSRF tokens. The outbox is one queue: claim() takes any pending row with no site or mode filter (mailer.py:73-91). In log mode, deliver() marks the row sent with provider 'log' and keeps its payload (mailer.py:178-186). The sender runs on every instance with the switch, the worker and email enabled (main.py:277-278). config.py:136-138 allows log mode with the switch on when EDGE_ENVIRONMENT is dev or local. dev is the default (config.py:49, :102) and the documented value (README.md:569). The user's decision of 2026-11-19 (EXEC.md on p3c-int e953f706, 'Production environment') puts the live website in the same Railway environment dev. Its consequences list names database changes, shared services and the background loops, not these settings.
findings.evidence: Code lines above. The EXEC 'Production environment' section is read at e953f706 (git show e953f706:EXEC.md, lines 15973-16030).
findings.failure_scenario: The live service is made as a copy of edge-bff. Different EDGE_MFA_KEY values: the admin's one enrolment works on one site only, and enrolling on the other replaces the nonce and breaks the first. Different EDGE_SESSION_SECRET values: each site counts sign-in failures for the same login separately, doubling the 10-per-15-min limit. Mismatched email modes: a beta with EDGE_EMAIL_MODE log and the switch on claims live users' code emails, marks them sent without sending them, and keeps the codes readable in the row. A live copy with EDGE_ENVIRONMENT dev and the mode unset (log) passes the start check, so registrations answer 202 while no email leaves.
findings.general_class: Per-service configuration that keys or routes shared rows, in a design where two service versions share one database. Same class: EDGE_OWNER/EDGE_LOGIN/EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER for the seed (C2-SKEW F2 covers the verifier overwrite), EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS, and any later secret-keyed column (Phase 5 webhook secrets, payment idempotency).
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c reads none of these settings. Its gateway key and owner headers are per edge-bff service, but terminal-api's rows are keyed by the owner key, not by a secret.
findings.affects_beta_live: Appears only with two websites on one database. Decide per setting whether both sites share it (MFA key, code secret, session secret) or must differ, and give the outbox (email mode) to exactly one resend-mode sender.
findings.fix: Add these settings to EXEC's beta/live consequences list with a decision for each. Make the log-mode guard independent of the environment name, for example by refusing log mode with the switch on unless EDGE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN is a Railway address, or with an explicit EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED. Record the outcome in RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md when the live service is created.
findings.confirm_check: When the live service is planned, compare the names (never values) of these variables on edge-bff and the live copy (railway variables --kv, names and equality only), and run the admin's TOTP on both sites.

findings.title: L4: no account-deletion path or procedure is recorded, and a deletion would leave every owner_key row (no FK by design), Orc's conversations and, with 3c, the terminal owner row and its audit
findings.root_cause: CONTRACT 1:53 says 'Existing owner_key columns get no foreign key in Phase 1'. CONTRACT 10 lists the Phase 4 admin actions (disable/enable, plan, revoke sessions, resend a code) without any deletion. The only DELETE of users is for pending rows (accounts.py:251, auth_flows.py:237). Rows cascaded by a users deletion: identities, email_codes, sessions (20261116_003:96,114,132), mfa_totp and mfa_recovery_codes (:143,152), user_capability_overrides and subscriptions (20261117_003:74,88). Rows kept, keyed by owner_key with no FK: jobs (with input.message, the question text, 20261008_002:27), conversation_ui, backtest jobs/results/trials (20261026_005:25,78), screener_items and watchlist (20261028_001:28,47), terminal_layouts, indicator_presets, terminal_drawings, watchlist_lists and items, user_preferences. Also kept: the outbox rows (L1), admin_audit with SET NULL (R1-42), Orc's conversations under the owner key and, from 3c, terminal.subscriber's owner row (never deleted, expires 2100-01-01) with 90 days of terminal.access_log (p3c-int 20261118_100). The README (493) already asks for an operational retention policy for job inputs; the Privacy and Terms content is out of this execution (EXEC.md:15407).
findings.evidence: grep of the migrations for REFERENCES edge_bff.users and owner_key columns (listed above); grep of apps/edge-bff/app for DELETE FROM edge_bff.users (pending only); CONTRACT 10.
findings.failure_scenario: After switch-on a paying user asks for their account and data to be deleted. The operator deletes the users row. The cascades remove the login, but the questions, backtests, screens, watchlists, layouts, drawings, preferences, Orc's conversations, the outbox addresses and (3c) the terminal owner row stay, orphaned under an owner key nobody can trace back. The admin_audit rows lose their target (R1-42). R1-42's option 'purge skips accounts the audit names' would block even the pending purge.
findings.general_class: Owner-keyed stores without referential links: every new owned kind (3e examples, Phase 4 usage counters, Phase 5 payment orders and events, 3c terminal rows in another schema) needs its place in one deletion procedure.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c adds one more owner-keyed store (terminal.subscriber kind owner and its access_log) to the list, but nothing it builds depends on a deletion procedure.
findings.affects_beta_live: No change: one database, one set of rows.
findings.fix: Record a deletion procedure, or a Phase 4 'delete account' action with a reason and audit, listing every owner-keyed store across edge_bff, Orc and terminal. Decide retention for jobs.input and the outbox (L1), and pseudonymise rather than null the audit ids (R1-42). Add the list to CONTRACT 1 or 10 so each new owned kind adds its line.
findings.confirm_check: Records: CONTRACT 10 and EXEC name the procedure; a test can later walk information_schema for owner_key columns and require each in the procedure's list.

findings.title: L5: every EDGE page, the sign-in page included, sends each visitor's IP address and user agent to Google Fonts, and no record lists this or the other recipients of personal data (Resend, the bucket host) for the Privacy text
findings.root_cause: static/index.html:16 imports https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter, and every Vite app's index.html does the same. The CSPs allow fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (main.py:60-63, :85-88, :372), so the shell's /login and /register pages contact Google before anyone signs in. Resend receives every address and email body (mailer.py:190-193). The Terminal, Backtest and Watchlist pages fetch presigned files from *.t3.storageapi.dev directly (main.py:60-63). The Pwned Passwords check sends only a 5-hex SHA-1 prefix (passwords.py:35-42; not personal). EXEC.md:15407 keeps the Privacy and Terms text out of this execution as the user's content, and no record lists these recipients.
findings.evidence: grep -n fonts.googleapis apps/edge-bff/static/index.html apps/edge-bff/*/index.html; CSP strings in main.py.
findings.failure_scenario: At switch-on the public sign-in and registration pages pass every visitor's IP address and user agent to Google, with no notice and before any consent. The Privacy text the user will write has no list of recipients to state.
findings.general_class: Third-party requests from pages and services that carry personal data: fonts, the email provider, the bucket provider, and later payment providers (Phase 5) and any analytics or CDN a page adds.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c relays the cut through edge-bff, which reduces the bucket requests for capped principals; it adds no third party.
findings.affects_beta_live: The live site at the user's domain is the public one, so this applies there first.
findings.fix: Self-host the Inter font (one family; font-src 'self'), or record Google Fonts as a recipient. Write the list of recipients (Resend: address and body; bucket host: IP and object keys; Google: IP and user agent, unless self-hosted) into EXEC or CONTRACT for the Privacy text.
findings.confirm_check: Records: the recipient list exists, or grep finds no fonts.googleapis.com in apps/edge-bff and the CSPs.

findings.title: L6: password verifiers use scrypt N=2^14, r=8, p=1, below OWASP's minimum equivalent (p=5 at this N), and the contract records no decision on it
findings.root_cause: security.py:140-147 derives every verifier with hashlib.scrypt(n=16384, r=8, p=1). The OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet's scrypt minimum is N=2^17, r=8, p=1, or an equivalent: N=2^16 p=2, N=2^15 p=3, N=2^14 p=5. CONTRACT section 4 says only 'stored with scrypt as today'. It records the length decision against NIST/OWASP (8 instead of 15) but no cost decision.
findings.evidence: Measured here: 46 ms per derivation at p=1, 175 ms at p=5, 330 ms at N=2^16 p=2. Each switch-on sign-in derives 1 + PENDING_CHECKED = 4 times (main.py:606-618), so p=5 costs about 0.7 s of CPU per sign-in.
findings.failure_scenario: A database leak with the switch on exposes the verifiers of every account to offline guessing at about 5 times the rate OWASP's minimum allows. 8-character passwords are allowed, which makes the margin smaller still.
findings.general_class: Security parameters inherited from the single-user design ('as today') without a recorded decision once real accounts arrive, such as the scrypt cost and the dummy-verify padding count.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c reads no verifier.
findings.affects_beta_live: No change.
findings.fix: User decision: raise the cost (for example p=5 at N=2^14, with rehash on the next successful sign-in, keeping the 1+3 padded derivations within the CPU budget), or record the current cost as accepted beside the length decision in CONTRACT 4.
findings.confirm_check: Records: CONTRACT 4 names the cost, or a test asserts the parameters of password_verifier.

checked: Branch r2-life from ae9a1d8f; read r1_seen.json (46 findings, 52 refuter notes) and r1_checked.json, so the findings above are new: outbox retention, log mode and emails were checked in round 1 only for delivery, not retention; R1-42 is about audit provenance, not leftover data.
CONTRACT.md sections 0-16, 8a and 8b; EXEC-MU-ACCOUNTS through 'Production environment' (e953f706 on p3c-int); README account and email sections; ERRORS M468-M482 entries referenced by the code.

Email address: users.email (lower, partial unique users_email_one_account), the outbox to_email (kept for ever, L1), email_suppression (kept on purpose), the throttle key hashes HMAC'd with EDGE_SESSION_SECRET and purged after 2 days. The mailer's log line masks the address outside local (first letter + ***@domain). No edge-bff log line carries an address except through L2. The page keeps the email typed into /register and /verify in memory only (index.html:11634-11635), never in storage or the URL.

Phone and names: written only at registration (auth_flows.py:199-203) after normalisation that matches every DB CHECK (E.164 regex; names via split/join matching btrim and char_length; email lower/strip matching lower(btrim) and the 254 bound). Deleted with a pending row after 24 h. Never logged, never sent to Orc, the workers or terminal-api. No list shows them yet (masking in lists is Phase 4, not built).

IP address: client_address is right-most X-Forwarded-For. It is stored only as an HMAC in auth_throttle (2-day purge) and sessions.created_ip_hash (deleted with the session). uvicorn runs with --no-access-log and --no-proxy-headers (Dockerfile:97). terminal-api's access_log.ip records edge-bff's private address for gateway calls. User agent: not collected anywhere.

Codes: 6 digits from secrets, HMAC-SHA256 with EDGE_CODE_SECRET per purpose and user, compared in constant time; plaintext only in the outbox payload. In resend mode the payload is nulled on sent, final failure, expired and suppressed (mailer.py:77-114). In log mode it is kept by design (dev); expired codes are useless, so no separate finding. Recovery codes: HMAC with EDGE_MFA_KEY, shown once, Cache-Control no-store by the middleware default. TOTP secret: derived, never stored; the enrol answer goes only to the page's memory and the QR is drawn locally (vendored qrcode-generator). Password verifiers: scrypt (L6). Session and registration tokens: 256-bit, only SHA-256 stored; Principal.token has repr=False; CSRF is an HMAC.

Logs, line by line: every logger call in apps/edge-bff/app (accounts, backtest, mailer, main, passwords, principal, screener, store, wake, worker) carries ids, classes, counts or masked text only. The loops redact database errors (worker.py:55-57, backtest.py failure_of). The request path does not (L2, verified under real uvicorn). Screener-worker logs an HMAC owner tag (screener.py:208-212), and the backtest worker receives no owner key. edge-bff sends Orc only X-Saniti-Owner. p3c-int terminal_access logs the owner key on an oversize header only.

Validation and error answers: validation_refusal names fields, never values; fields_of and invalid() name fields; the unexpected handler answers 503 without a body. No answer returns another owner's data: the PREFERENCE_CONFLICT and REVISION_CONFLICT bodies are the same owner's; the shared caches (models, catalog, page files, the screener reviews map) hold no personal data.

Deletion and cascades: users FKs (CASCADE: identities, email_codes, sessions, mfa_totp, mfa_recovery_codes, overrides, subscriptions; SET NULL: admin_audit, overrides.created_by); owner_key tables without FK (L4); a pending registration has no sessions, preferences or terminal rows; verify_registration deletes the other pending registrations of the address; sessions cleanup deletes expired sessions and those revoked more than a day ago.

Readers outside edge-bff: pgweb holds only edge_bff.jobs (state, updated_at); sync_database_schema reads public only; the AI roles have no edge_bff grant; telegram-monitor reads no edge-bff data or logs; scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py prints the user id and counts and writes counts-only audit rows; restart_postgres counts jobs.

Browser storage: the registry classes; sign-out clears every user key, the IndexedDB caches and the last-login mark; a change of identity clears the previous account's keys. The edge-last-login mark holds owner:<key>, a pseudonymous identifier, and stays after a session merely expires (not reported). The MFA enrolment, recovery codes and auth-flow email stay in memory only.

3c (p3c-int 41067e7d): owner rows use a synthetic address (sha256 prefix of the owner key) and 'EDGE owner <key>', never sign in, and are made only for signed-in principals; access_log.version is checked by pattern; the cut relay answers Cache-Control private; nothing in 3c changes mailer, accounts, store or the unexpected handler, and both new tests fail the same way on a git-archive extract of 41067e7d.

Tests run on my cluster r2_life (port 55534, now stopped): test_r2_life.py 2 failed as intended; with test_auth_flows, test_auth_throttle and test_principal, 81 passed; with test_auth_pages_live (EDGE_TEST_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome), 4 passed; all 694 tests collect. The p3c-int extract was deleted after the run. Nothing pushed, deployed or run against Railway.

findings.affects_3c_why: The Monitor is not part of 3c; the Terminal frame uses the shared module's accessText.
findings.affects_beta_live: The same on both sites. On the live site the first users are non-admin accounts, so this is the first screen they see.
findings.fix: In edge-client.js api(), make the thrown error's message the person's words (info.message, else EdgeLabels.access or accessText) and keep the code in .info.code. Alternatively, the Monitor shows e.text || e.info?.message. Until the 3e example mode exists, a principal without monitor.view should land on the first tab its access holds, not on /monitor.
findings.related_r1: R1-19 (the same contract gap on the drawings client); this mechanism and site are not covered.

findings.title: Every CAPABILITY_REQUIRED and LIMIT_REACHED carries one fixed sentence per code, so the name, limit and wait stay in details that no page shows; the email-code and MFA throttles even tell the person to upgrade a plan
findings.root_cause: errors.refusal (errors.py:107) sets the message to message_of(code) (errors.py:101). That is one sentence per code (MESSAGES :14 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, :17 LIMIT_REACHED), whatever the details hold. Both clients show the server's sentence first: accessText (edge-session.ts:341-350, `e.message || <sentence built from display_name or retryAfter>`) and the shell's authText (index.html:11637, `info.message || EdgeLabels.auth.errors[code]`). So details.display_name (M481 C1 F3) and the limit, allowed and retry_after_s of the queue cap (M481 C3 F1) never reach the person. The auth throttles reuse the plan code LIMIT_REACHED: code_tries at auth_flows.py:422 and mfa_tries at :552. They therefore say "You have reached your plan's limit ... upgrade the plan", and the shell's correct label at edge-labels.js:208 is never shown.
findings.evidence:
Four failing tests in tests/test_c2web_browser.py:
- test_c2web_w2_too_many_wrong_email_codes: 20 wrong /password/reset codes get the plan sentence.
- test_c2web_w2_too_many_wrong_mfa_codes: 10 wrong /mfa/verify codes get the same sentence.
- test_c2web_w2_a_capability_refusal: a paid account with radar.view overridden false gets details.display_name 'Radar', but accessText(readError(real answer)) in Chromium is 'This feature is not part of your EDGE plan...'.
- test_c2web_w2_the_queued_backtest_limit: backtest.queued_jobs 1, second submit; the page text is the generic plan sentence.
Mutation check: wording the message from details in errors.refusal makes all four pass.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. After 20 wrong email codes on /verify or /reset, a person who is not signed in and has no plan reads "upgrade the plan". The real way out is to wait up to 24 h.
2. After 10 wrong authenticator codes on /mfa, the admin is told to upgrade a plan, and the 15-minute wait is not named.
3. A plan without the Radar opens the Radar tab and reads "This feature...".
4. A second queued backtest gets no mention of backtests, of the limit 1, or of the 30 s wait.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c builds its ticker, data-set and history refusals with capability_required and its quota-0 refusal with LIMIT_REACHED. They reach the Terminal through accessText, so the display_name the 3c contract says it sends ('Terminal tickers', 'Terminal data sets') is never shown. A fix in errors.refusal or accessText needs no 3c change, so it does not block building 3c.
findings.affects_beta_live: The same on both sites.
findings.related_r1: R1-34 (worker messages relayed verbatim) and R1-9 (SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT understates the wait). Their fixes cover worker-written messages and the sign-in limit, not edge-bff's own sentence per code or accessText's order.

findings.title: The shell's own session (Edge.auth, the model list) never follows a change of plan: edge-client.js ignores X-Edge-Entitlements and the frames' 'entitlements' broadcast
findings.root_cause: CONTRACT 12 says the X-Edge-Entitlements header makes EDGE read the session again. The shell's client, edge-client.js api(), never reads that header and subscribes only to onCleared (edge-client.js:17). The shared module's 'entitlements' handling (edge-session.ts:414, :432) invalidates only the module's own clients. Edge.auth (the session answer with its access object) and the model list (loaded once per session) therefore stay as the sign-in read them.
findings.evidence: tests/test_c2web_browser.py::test_c2web_w3: a paid account signs in, then an override takes backtest.view away. The server's header changes from db-c85446158b5a to db-5021f27cf6c6. After a shell call and an 'entitlements' broadcast, Edge.auth.access.version is still db-c85446158b5a and its capabilities still list backtest.view.
findings.failure_scenario: A plan is narrowed or raised (Phase 4 admin) or expires while a tab is open. The shell keeps the old access and model list until a reload. A model the plan lost is still offered and then refused at submit (shown as a bare code, see the Monitor finding). 3e decisions taken from Edge.auth.access (Monitor example mode, the mode each frame loads in, lock prompts in the shell) would follow the old plan.
findings.general_class: State that depends on the plan, held in memory by a page that does not use the shared session client: the shell's Edge.auth and models, and later the /admin and /pay shell pages. It differs from R1-38, which is the Screener boot cache keyed by data version.
findings.affects_3c_why: The 3c Terminal frame uses the shared module, which does read the header.
findings.affects_beta_live: An open tab of either site keeps the plan it signed in with. With M479 (old shell code in open tabs), a tab can hold both old code and old access.
findings.fix: Send edge-client.js api() through EdgeSession.edge.send, or read the header there. On a version change, its own or broadcast, read /api/v1/auth/session again into auth, drop the model list and dispatch edge-auth.
findings.related_r1: The R1 refuter note C:spec (edge-session.ts:429-432 only re-reads the session) concerns cache pointers, not the shell's session object.

findings.title: A session that ends under a tab's frame leaves the shell signed in: the frame gets 401 and says 'sign in again', and nothing tells the shell
findings.root_cause: CONTRACT 3 says a 401 UNAUTHENTICATED sends the person to sign-in. On a 401, send() only invalidates its own client (edge-session.ts:509). No signed-out message exists: the channel carries only 'entitlements' and 'cleared', and there is no parent postMessage. The shell resets only on its own 401 or on 'cleared'. Each frame shows only its own sentence (radar/src/api.ts:17, overview/src/api.ts:18, watchlist/src/api.ts:16, and the SIGN_IN texts of the Terminal and Backtest).
findings.evidence: tests/test_c2web_browser.py::test_c2web_w4: a stand-in frame page uses /edge-session.js like every tab. The sessions are revoked, then the Terminal tab is opened. The frame is answered 401, and 2 s later the shell still shows the signed-in workspace with no Login field.
findings.failure_scenario: With the switch on, a session ends after 8 h idle, or through sign-out-all, a password reset or a disable on another device. The person opens the Radar tab and reads 'Your EDGE session ended. Sign in again, then open the Radar.' No sign-in is on screen; the rail and the account menu stay up, and the person must find Sign out or reload.
findings.general_class: A session outcome inside a frame that the shell never learns: 401, the synthetic USER_CHANGED and MFA_REQUIRED. The same applies to every tab, the 3e example frames and later the Phase 4 and 5 pages.
findings.affects_3c_why: The 3c Terminal frame meets it like every other tab, but 3c does not change it.
findings.affects_beta_live: There is one sessions table, so sign-out-all or a password reset on one site also ends the sessions of the other. A person using both sites meets this path often.
findings.fix: On a 401 of the page's own account, the shared module posts {type:'signed-out'} on the channel (and to the parent window). The shell resets to the sign-in page on it, keeping pending writes stamped as the module already does.
findings.related_r1: R1-1 covers a different 401: terminal-api's own 401 relayed to a signed-in user.

findings.title: Registration stores first and last names with markup, bidi overrides, invisible and control characters and formula prefixes, and the contract has no rule for showing them to another account (Phase 4)
findings.root_cause: checked_name (auth_flows.py:103-107) only collapses whitespace and checks 1 to 100 characters. fields_of refuses only NUL and unpaired surrogates. CONTRACT sections 1 and 10 give the columns and the Phase 4 list, but no rule on characters or output encoding.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe on my cluster, not committed: POST /api/v1/auth/register with first_name '‮nimda​' and last_name '=HYPERLINK("https://evil.example","x")\x07' answered 202, and edge_bff.users holds both values unchanged. No page or email shows names today (grep of app/ and static/), so nothing is exploitable now.
findings.failure_scenario: The Phase 4 admin list (CONTRACT 10) or the audit view shows a name that a right-to-left override renders as 'admin'. An export opened in a spreadsheet runs the formula. A later email that greets by name carries the markup.
findings.general_class: Free text from one account shown to another: the Phase 4 admin list, detail and audit, Phase 5 receipts, and any email by name. Usernames are safe ([a-z0-9_]).
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c shows no names.
findings.affects_beta_live: None.
findings.fix: Add a contract rule for names before Phase 4: NFKC-normalise; refuse Unicode categories Cc and Cf (bidi overrides, zero-width characters); encode on output (the shell's element() already uses text nodes); quote a leading = + - @ in any export.

findings.title: The shell's CSP keeps script-src 'unsafe-inline' for its two inline scripts (the app is about 2,600 lines inline) and has no form-action, and the shell is the page that will host the Phase 4 admin views of other users' data
findings.root_cause: The default policy at main.py:372 is "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'", with no form-action, because index.html carries inline scripts at :6 and :11061. The tab apps already run with script-src 'self'.
findings.evidence: main.py:372, and the grep of index.html (inline <script> at lines 6 and 11061). I found no HTML sink in the shell today: element() writes text nodes (index.html:11141-11185), and the only innerHTML is a fixed icon (:13021). So this is defence in depth, not an exploit.
findings.failure_scenario: In Phase 4 the /admin page in the shell lists other accounts' names, emails and phones. One innerHTML or an attribute sink added there by mistake becomes script execution in an MFA-passed admin session, and the CSP cannot stop it.
findings.general_class: Every page that shows data from other accounts or providers: the Phase 4 /admin page, the Phase 5 /pay page and the 3e Monitor examples, all in the shell.
findings.affects_3c_why: The Terminal app's policy has no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.
findings.affects_beta_live: None.
findings.fix: Before Phase 4, move both inline scripts to /edge-app.js (the preview tool inlines files anyway), drop 'unsafe-inline' from script-src, and add form-action 'self'.

findings.title: No page offers the Phase 1 password change or sign-out everywhere
findings.root_cause: POST /api/v1/auth/password/change and /sign-out-all are built (auth_flows.py) and listed in CONTRACT 4, but nothing in static/ calls them. The account menu (index.html:11551-11563) offers only settings and Sign out. CONTRACT 12's page list names neither.
findings.evidence: grep of static/ for password/change and sign-out-all finds nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A person who thinks a session was stolen, or who wants to rotate a password, can do it only through a reset by email code ('Forgot password?'). The admin needs a working mailbox to change the admin password.
findings.general_class: Routes built without a page: the Phase 4 email change (email_codes purpose email_change) and session lists are the next ones.
findings.affects_3c_why: No 3c path is involved.
findings.affects_beta_live: sign-out-all would end the sessions of both sites (one table); its wording should say so.
findings.fix: Add an account page in the shell (contract 12 route table) for password change and sign-out everywhere, worded in edge-labels.js, or record the decision to rely on the reset.

findings.title: No Strict-Transport-Security on any EDGE answer: the first visit to the live domain can be stripped to HTTP on the sign-in and registration pages
findings.root_cause: The protections middleware (main.py:361-372) sets nosniff, Referrer-Policy and the CSP but never Strict-Transport-Security. No file in the repository mentions HSTS. Settings.validate requires an https origin and Secure cookies, which protect the cookie but not the first page load.
findings.evidence: grep -ri strict-transport over the repository finds nothing. I did not check whether Railway's edge adds the header (no calls to Railway were allowed).
findings.failure_scenario: On the live custom domain, a person types the domain or follows an http link on a hostile network. Without HSTS the first request can be answered by an attacker's HTTP copy of /login or /register, which collects the password.
findings.general_class: Transport headers that no service sets: edge-bff, and terminal-api if it ever gets a public domain again.
findings.affects_3c_why: No 3c path is involved.
findings.affects_beta_live: It matters most for the live site on the user's domain. The Railway address may be covered by Railway's edge, which is unchecked.
findings.confirm_check: Run curl -sI https://edge-bff-dev.up.railway.app/login (and the live domain once it is set) and look for Strict-Transport-Security. If it is absent, set it in protections (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains only after listing the domain's other hosts).
findings.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security on every answer when EDGE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN is https; consider preload once the live domain is final.

findings.title: On the live custom domain, sibling hosts are same-site: the session and registration cookies lack the __Host- prefix (cookie tossing), and SameSite=Strict GETs from a sibling can spend 3c's per-owner Terminal quota
findings.root_cause: The cookies are named edge_session and edge_registration (main.py:659, auth_flows.py:406 and :415), host-only, without the __Host- prefix. Starlette keeps the last of two cookies with one name (checked: cookie_parser('edge_session=a; edge_session=b') gives b). A cookie set by a sibling with Domain=<registrable domain> and Path=/ after the victim's sign-in is sent after it and wins. SameSite=Strict does not separate hosts of one site, so a sibling page's GET subresources carry the session.
findings.evidence: Code and parser behaviour as above. On the beta, up.railway.app is on the Public Suffix List (checked in the local copy of the list), so no sibling exists there. The exposure depends on the live domain's other hosts, which are not chosen yet.
findings.failure_scenario: Another host under the user's domain is compromised or taken over: a marketing site, or a dangling CNAME. - It sets edge_session to the attacker's token, so the person works inside the attacker's account (login CSRF). - With 3c, its requests to /api/terminal/v1/manifest/ or reference/ carry the person's session and use up that owner's own quota (D6: 60 tickers per hour, 300 files per hour). The person then gets LIMIT_REACHED.
findings.general_class: Any state kept in a cookie or reached by a GET with a cookie, on a domain that hosts other sites. The POST writes are still protected by the Origin check.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c makes each Terminal GET count against the owner's own quota, so same-site GETs become a way to block a person's Terminal. Before 3c they counted against the one gateway account.
findings.affects_beta_live: It appears only on the live site at the user's domain; the beta on the Railway address is cross-site to every other host.
findings.confirm_check: When the live domain is chosen, list every host under its registrable domain. If any host other than EDGE serves content, rename the cookies __Host-edge_session and __Host-edge_registration (the latter needs Path=/), or put EDGE on a registrable domain of its own.
findings.fix: Use the __Host- prefix (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) for both cookies, and keep EDGE alone on its registrable domain.

findings.title: Two edge-bff services on one database share every claim loop: the email sender, the AI job worker, the backtest loop and the hourly cleanup take any row, whichever site queued it
findings.evidence: The claim SQL as cited. The impact depends on how beta and live are configured, which is still open.
findings.failure_scenario: The beta runs EDGE_EMAIL_MODE=log, a natural choice for a test site. A person registers on the live site, and the beta's sender claims the code email and only logs it, so /verify waits for a code that never comes. Or an older live worker dispatches a job the newer beta queued, with a payload or principal rule the old code does not know.
findings.general_class: Background loops over shared tables in a multi-version deployment: every SKIP LOCKED claim and every cleanup.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c adds no claim loop.
findings.affects_beta_live: It appears only with two edge-bff services on one database.
findings.confirm_check: With two services on one database, queue a code email from one service and read which instance's log carries email_logged or email_sent for that outbox_id. In the beta/live design, decide whether only one service runs the loops (EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED false on the other) or whether rows carry their site.
findings.fix: In the beta/live design, run the loops in one service only (switches off on the other) and record it in the runbook. Or stamp each queued row with its site and claim only its own.

checked: Read r1_seen.json (46 findings and the refuter notes) first. Everything above is new, or a site that the round-1 entry and its fix do not cover; each finding names the related entry.

CSRF: listed all 110 routes from app.routes with their dependencies (scratch script). Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE uses auth.writer or need(write=True), except the unauthenticated auth routes (sign-in, register, verify, resend, forgot, reset; Origin check only) and the hook. The Origin check (main.py:337-343) refuses a missing or foreign Origin. The hook prefix skips it, and its only route verifies the Svix signature (R1-15 covers the route walk). GET handlers in main, backtest, screener, pages, preferences and catalog only read (the session touch excepted). HEAD runs the GET handler. There is no CORS, no JSONP and no method override.
Path tricks on the hook exemption: a %2f-encoded path under /api/v1/hooks/ is decoded by uvicorn but matches no route, so it does not reach another route.

Cookies: edge_session is HttpOnly, Secure (forced off local by Settings.validate), SameSite=Strict, Path=/, Max-Age 24 h. edge_registration is the same with Path /api/v1/auth/. Sign-in revokes the previous cookie's session, and passing MFA rotates the token. up.railway.app is on the Public Suffix List (local copy), so the beta has no same-site siblings.

Cache headers: every answer gets no-store by default (main.py:364). Page files use private, no-cache with an ETag, and the 304 on ?sha= comes only after the capability dependency (pages.py). Screener documents carry an ETag per filtered document plus no-store. The SSE stream is no-store. App assets are public and immutable but hold no data (3f covers lab code). Model logos and favicons are public files from the repository. Terminal logos are private with a max-age from terminal-api (public issuer art). On p3c-int the cut relay forces private.

Clickjacking: frame-ancestors 'self' on every policy. The early-return answers (ORIGIN_REJECTED, REQUEST_TOO_LARGE, the 503 handler) are JSON without a CSP, which is harmless. The postMessage listeners check origin and source (index.html:11410-11415, terminal stats.ts:35-39).

Open redirects: no next or return parameter anywhere. go() accepts only ROUTES. The branch tab opens staticUrl of an internal route. Edge.safeUrl allows only http and https and refuses *.railway.internal. No page sets location.href or calls window.open with outside input.

HTML injection: usernames are limited to [a-z0-9_]. Emails (email_texts.py) carry no user-chosen text and escape the code. The shell builds the DOM with text nodes (element()). The sampled tab sinks for saved names escape them (layouts.ts esc, screener app.ts esc(S.name), indicators escH). No name of one account is shown to another today. Names are recorded for Phase 4 in the names finding.
Served SVGs (model logos, favicon, edge-logo) contain no script or event handlers. No service worker exists anywhere.

Preferences sync (edge-session.ts load) writes only registry sync keys into storage, so a server key cannot plant edge-last-login or other keys. The storage registry, the cleared broadcast and the identity marks were checked against M473/M478 and R1-20.

Refusal handling per page:
- Radar, Overview, Watchlist, Backtest and Terminal use accessText for access refusals (see the wording finding).
- The account pages use authText: CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED, USERNAME_TAKEN, MFA_LOCKED, MFA_NOT_ENROLLED and PASSWORD_BREACHED are worded and have a way out (Resend, setup, Forgot password, Back to sign in). LIMIT_REACHED is not (see the wording finding).

- CSRF_INVALID is retried once.
- The Monitor shows bare codes (see the Monitor finding).

findings.title: A failing hourly cleanup stops every queued AI run: the worker never reaches the claim, and Phases 0/1 put two purges in that one 5 s transaction
findings.root_cause: Worker.run (worker.py:44-59) runs Store.cleanup_sessions and store.claim in one try block. cleaned_at is set only after the cleanup succeeds (:49). When the cleanup raises, the except branch (:57) sleeps poll_seconds and the next turn runs the cleanup again, so the claim (:50) is never reached. cleanup_sessions (store.py:354-358) is one transaction under the store's SET LOCAL statement_timeout '5s' (store.py:53). Phase 0 added purge_throttle (throttle.py:122-125) to it and Phase 1 added purge_pending (accounts.py:248-251). Both purges grow with unauthenticated traffic: typed logins and registrations.
findings.evidence: Test tests/test_c2_ops_recheck.py::test_a_failing_hourly_cleanup_does_not_stop_the_run_queue fails: '1376 cleanups in 2 s and no claim'. A real trigger, measured on my cluster (PG16, shared_buffers 128 MB): the cleanup SQL as the worker runs it, with 100k sessions, 107k email_codes, 50k admin_audit, 20k subscriptions and 5000 pending accounts older than 24 h, fails with 'canceling statement due to statement timeout', CONTEXT DELETE FROM ONLY edge_bff.email_codes WHERE $1 = user_id, after 5000.6 ms. The sessions and throttle deletes of the same transaction roll back with it. See finding 2 for why the purge is about 25 ms per account.
findings.failure_scenario: A sign-up campaign or a bot registers about 200 or more addresses that never verify (register needs no session; SEND_IP is not enforced). 24 h later the purge passes the 5 s limit. From then on the worker runs the failing cleanup about every 2 s, each time burning up to 5 s of database time. No queued Monitor run is ever dispatched, and expired sessions and throttle rows are no longer purged. The pending backlog only grows, because every purge rolls back. With the switch off the same happens once auth_throttle grows past what one 5 s delete can remove (see finding 5). /ready keeps answering 200.
findings.general_class: Background maintenance coupled to the primary work of the same loop: one try block and one transaction, so any maintenance statement that fails (a timeout, a lock wait, a grant missing after a migration, a constraint) stops the primary work and rolls back the other purges. The same coupling is in BacktestLoop.run (backtest.py:787-795): store.prune and store.reap run before store.claim in one try, so a failing prune stops every backtest. Any later purge added to cleanup_sessions inherits it: email_codes, email_outbox, Phase 4 account deletion, Phase 5 payment reconciliation.
findings.affects_3c_why: p3c-int (41067e7d) leaves worker.py, store.py, accounts.py and throttle.py unchanged. 3c adds nothing to the cleanup, and the Terminal path does not depend on the AI queue.
findings.affects_beta_live: Worse with two edge-bff services: both run the same purges on the same rows. The second DELETE of a pending account waits on the first one's row locks inside its own 5 s limit, so concurrent purges time out sooner, and both services' AI queues stop together, since the data is shared.
findings.fix: Run each purge in its own transaction and its own try, apart from the claim. Set cleaned_at, or a per-purge next-attempt time with backoff, even when a purge fails, so the claim is always reached. Purge in bounded batches (e.g. DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ... LIMIT 500)) and log the failure by its class. Do the same for BacktestLoop.run's prune and reap.
findings.confirm_check: Run the test above; its control (a cleanup that succeeds) is the existing test_edge.py::test_sessions_are_cleaned_when_the_loop_starts_whatever_the_clock_reads.

findings.title: No index on the foreign keys to edge_bff.users: the pending purge costs about 25 ms per account (200 accounts = 5 s), and every request of an account without a live plan scans all subscriptions
findings.root_cause: Six FK columns that reference edge_bff.users(user_id) have no index whose leading column they are: sessions.user_id (20261116_003 ALTER TABLE sessions ADD user_id ... ON DELETE CASCADE), email_codes.user_id (only the partial email_codes_one_live WHERE consumed_at IS NULL), admin_audit.actor_user_id and target_user_id (SET NULL), subscriptions.user_id (only the partial subscriptions_one_active WHERE status='active'; 20261117_003:86-100), and user_capability_overrides.created_by_user_id. Both migrations decided 'no index beyond keys' on CONTRACT section 1's 'users and sessions number in the thousands at most'. But each deleted account fires one cascade or SET NULL query per referencing table, and every non-indexed one is a full scan. The same missing indexes serve the principal's hot reads: create_session's cap (accounts.py:226) and revoke_all (:238-241), the reset and change revokes (auth_flows.py), and the resolve/owner GRANTS 'lapsed' CTE (accounts.py:49-52). The lapsed CTE runs for every account without a live subscription and filters subscriptions by user_id with status 'expired' or ended, which the partial index cannot serve.
findings.evidence: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on my cluster with 20k active and 7k pending accounts, 100k sessions, 107k codes, 50k audit and 20k subscriptions. DELETE of 200 pending accounts took 5002 ms, with these trigger times: email_codes_user_id_fkey 1709.5 ms, sessions_user_id_fkey 1877.6 ms, admin_audit_actor 543.3 ms, admin_audit_target 601.5 ms, subscriptions_user_id_fkey 242.1 ms, each over 200 calls. The indexed ones (identities, mfa_totp, mfa_recovery_codes) took 2-8 ms in total. The full resolve query of an account whose subscription ended: 'Seq Scan on subscriptions s_2 ... Rows Removed by Filter: 19999', 3.2 ms, against 0.34 ms with a live subscription. create_session's cap UPDATE: 'Seq Scan on sessions ... Rows Removed by Filter: 99995', 13.1 ms, 2041 buffers. revoke_all: Seq Scan, 8.7 ms. pending_logins (every switch-on sign-in) does a Seq Scan on users, 2.5 ms, because 20261117_002 dropped users_email_key and the partial users_email_one_account (status <> 'pending') cannot serve status='pending'. Test tests/test_c2_ops_recheck.py::test_every_reference_to_an_account_has_an_index fails and lists exactly these six columns.
findings.failure_scenario: With the switch on, about 200 unverified registrations in an hour (unauthenticated; any addresses) make the next day's hourly purge pass the 5 s statement timeout. The purge then fails every time (finding 1 turns this into a stopped AI queue). Separately, every request, Terminal call and SSE loop iteration of a free or lapsed user (the default plan, likely most users) scans the whole subscriptions table. Its cost grows with the subscription history Phase 5 adds (one row per period or renewal), and the worker's dispatch check (owner()) pays it too.
findings.general_class: A foreign key added without an index on the referencing column (or only a partial one), justified by a size assumption that holds for the referenced table but not for the referencing ones. Postgres runs one scan of each referencing table per deleted parent row, and the principal's per-request reads go by the same column. It reaches every later delete of users (Phase 4 account deletion and disable cascades, admin tooling) and every later table that references users: Phase 5 payment_orders and payment_events, and 3e or Phase 4 audit-like tables (cf. R1-42, which covers what SET NULL rewrites but not its cost).
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c reads the same principal (resolve) per Terminal call, so default-plan users pay the subscriptions scan on every Terminal request. That is a cost, not a correctness defect 3c builds on. p3c-int adds no FK to users, and its terminal.subscriber.edge_owner_key is UNIQUE (indexed).
findings.affects_beta_live: Unchanged by two edge-bff versions. Both run the same purge and the same resolve against the one database, so the cost is paid twice.
findings.fix: A forward migration with plain btree indexes: sessions(user_id), email_codes(user_id), admin_audit(actor_user_id), admin_audit(target_user_id), subscriptions(user_id, starts_at DESC) and user_capability_overrides(created_by_user_id). Optionally users(email) WHERE status = 'pending' for pending_logins and verify_registration's delete. Record EXPLAIN evidence in DATABASE_CHANGELOG and correct CONTRACT section 1's sizing sentence.
findings.related_r1: R1-42 (admin_audit SET NULL rewrites rows): its fix (RESTRICT or no FK) changes the semantics but not the per-row scan of the other five columns, and it does not cover sessions, email_codes or subscriptions, nor the per-request subscriptions scan.
findings.confirm_check: Run the test; to reproduce the timing, fill the tables as in the evidence and run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) of purge_pending for 200 accounts.

findings.title: The email outbox is never purged (no DELETE grant), and its hot reads scan every email ever sent: the unauthenticated register/resend/forgot cooldown read and the sender's three claim statements every 5 s
findings.root_cause: email_outbox has only its PK and idempotency_key UNIQUE. GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON edge_bff.email_outbox (20261116_003:225) gives edge-bff no way to delete a row, and no purge exists. The payload is nulled after sending, but the row stays forever, with to_email, which is personal data. FlowStore._may_send (auth_flows.py:137-143) runs 'SELECT 1 FROM email_outbox WHERE to_email=%s AND created_at > now()-60s LIMIT 1' on every register, code/resend, password/forgot and sign-in restart, under the address's advisory lock. OutboxStore.claim (mailer.py:73-91) runs two UPDATEs and a SELECT filtered by status, expires_at and next_at on every sender turn: after each send, and every POLL_SECONDS = 5 s when idle. None of these has an index. email_codes rows of active accounts are also never purged: consumed codes stay until the account is deleted, and anyone who knows an address can add 10 a day through forgot. email_hook_events is GRANT SELECT, INSERT only (20261117_001:43), so it also grows forever, one row per Resend event.
findings.evidence: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) at 500k sent rows: _may_send does a Parallel Seq Scan (Rows Removed by Filter 166673 x3), 30.3 ms, 8367 buffers. The claim's UPDATE expired does a Seq Scan (Rows Removed 500020), 43.3 ms. The UPDATE suppressed does a Seq Scan, 45.4 ms. The SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED does a Seq Scan plus a Sort, 54.1 ms. Each statement reads 8367 buffers (65 MB). Test tests/test_c2_ops_recheck.py::test_the_outbox_reads_of_every_send_and_every_sender_turn_use_an_index records the real SQL of OutboxStore.claim and FlowStore._may_send and EXPLAINs it at 20k sent rows. It fails on all four statements. Its control (a scratch run adding (to_email, created_at) and a partial (next_at) WHERE status IN ('pending','sending')) passes, so the test can be made to pass.
findings.failure_scenario: After the switch goes on, every email ever sent stays in the outbox. The sender scans all of it three times every 5 s on each instance, about 150 ms and 200 MB of buffer reads per poll at 500k rows, growing linearly. Every unauthenticated register or forgot request does one more full scan while holding the address lock. A script sending forgot requests for known addresses (10 per address per day, inside the limits) adds an outbox row and an email_codes row each time, which speeds up both the growth and finding 2's purge cost. No retention ever removes the recipients' addresses.
findings.general_class: An append-only operational table with a status queue on top and no purge, no DELETE grant and no index for its queue or lookup reads: email_outbox, email_codes (consumed rows of active accounts), email_hook_events. Phase 5's payment_events and payment_orders, and any webhook dedup table, follow the same pattern unless each gets a retention purge and a queue index.
findings.affects_3c_why: The outbox is used only with the switch on, by the auth flows. p3c-int does not touch mailer.py, auth_flows.py or the outbox schema.
findings.affects_beta_live: Worse with two edge-bff services: each runs its own sender loop (SKIP LOCKED keeps sends single, but both scan the whole table every 5 s), so the scan load doubles.
findings.fix: A forward migration adding an index on (to_email, created_at) and a partial index on (next_at) WHERE status IN ('pending','sending'), plus a retention purge for sent, expired, failed and suppressed outbox rows, consumed or expired email_codes, and email_hook_events (needs a DELETE grant or a SECURITY DEFINER purge). Run the purge in its own transaction, not inside cleanup_sessions (finding 1). The retention period is a user decision: one day covers SEND_EMAIL's window; Resend's idempotency key lasts 24 h.
findings.confirm_check: Run the test; the retention part needs the user's retention decision before a test can lock it.

findings.title: A database error while edge-bff starts leaves the AI worker, the email sender and the hourly purges unstarted for the whole deployment, while /ready answers 200; EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED and EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED typos turn the loops off silently
findings.root_cause: lifespan (main.py:240-279) reads store.ready once. On any exception ready['value'] stays False, and with the switch on a failing seed_user or seed_plan also sets it False (:256, :271). The worker task, which also runs every purge, and the email task are created only when ready['value'] is true (:272, :277), and nothing retries. The /ready route (:400-405) calls store.ready again on every request, so it answers 200 as soon as the database is back. Railway's edge-bff healthcheck is /ready (railway.ts edge-bff healthcheck '/ready'), so the deploy is marked healthy. Separately, config.from_env parses EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED (config.py:109) and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED (:126) as 'anything but true is off', while EDGE_MULTIUSER uses switch_of (config.py:23-28: 'a typo must not turn accounts on'). validate never refuses EDGE_MULTIUSER=true with the sender off.
findings.evidence: tests/test_c2_ops_recheck.py, with BlipStore, a Store whose first ready() raises OperationalError('the database system is starting up'). (a) test_the_email_sender_runs_once_ready_answers_after_a_database_error_at_start: switch on, worker_enabled; /ready is 200 and register is 202, but the outbox row stays 'pending' after 5 s. (b) test_the_ai_worker_runs_once_ready_answers_after_a_database_error_at_start: switch off; /ready is 200 and the run is 202, but its state stays 'QUEUED'. (c) test_a_typo_in_a_loop_switch_stops_the_start[EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED|EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED]: from_env with 'ture' does not raise. Controls run in a scratch file and then removed: with failures=0 the same tests pass (the row becomes 'sent' and the run 'FINISHED').
findings.failure_scenario: A push to main deploys edge-bff while the planned 09:45 or 20:45 WIB Postgres restart, about 12 s, is running. restart_postgres.py guards against crons and running statements, not against deploys. A Postgres OOM restart can overlap a deploy the same way. The new container's lifespan meets the outage and the deploy still goes green. Until the next deploy, Monitor runs stay QUEUED ('Waiting'), expired sessions, throttle rows and pending accounts are never purged, and with the switch on no registration or reset code is ever sent. The answers still say CODE_SENT, so new users cannot register, and nothing alerts. The same silent state follows a typo such as EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED=True1.
findings.general_class: A background loop started once from the lifespan, gated by a readiness probe at boot, while the health route probes again on each call, so the health check cannot see that the loop is missing. This covers the AI worker, the email sender, the purges inside the worker, and any later loop started the same way (Phase 5 payment reconciliation, a 3e or Phase 4 admin job). It also covers lenient boolean parsing of switches that turn loops off.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c changes no lifespan or loop code (p3c-int main.py diff touches the Terminal routes only). The Terminal proxy needs no background loop.
findings.affects_beta_live: Worse with two services: each deploy, beta following main and live on 'push ke live', is another chance to start during a database restart. restart_postgres.py's edge_domain() and edge_ready() read only the service named 'edge-bff', so after a restart the live service's /ready is never checked. A second service set to run without loops, by intent or by typo, leaves the outbox to the other, and the two may run different versions.
findings.fix: Start the loops unconditionally and let each wait or retry for the database itself, the way the backtest loop already does, or retry the boot checks (seed, seed_plan) in the background. Make /ready report 503 while a configured loop has not started. Parse EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED with switch_of. Optionally log an error when EDGE_MULTIUSER=true runs with the sender off, so an intentional sender-less instance is visible.
findings.confirm_check: Run the three tests.

findings.title: Since Phase 0 nothing bounds sign-ins per client, and every password check runs on the default thread pool that every database call uses: a burst of sign-ins with made-up logins stalls the signed-in users and grows auth_throttle without bound
findings.root_cause: The sign-in (main.py:592-627) runs scrypt (security.py:14-15, n=16384 r=8, about 16 MiB each) through asyncio.to_thread: once with the switch off (:622), 1 + PENDING_CHECKED = 4 times with it on (:611-617). It uses the event loop's default executor, min(32, cpu+4) threads, the same pool every route's database call uses (principal.py:299/303 session resolve, the throttle, the stores). The only bound before the derivation is SIGNIN_LOGIN, per typed login (main.py:600); SIGNIN_IP is recorded but not enforced (throttle.py:31). So a client that types a different login each time is never refused. Before Phase 0, the in-process limiter (98be0931^ main.py:512-524) allowed 5 failures per minute per request.client.host. Behind Railway with --no-proxy-headers that host is the proxy, so the old limit was effectively global, and it was replaced without any per-client or global bound. Each made-up login also inserts its own auth_throttle row (attempt -> _add, plus a signin_ip row). The migration's sizing comment ('the purge ... reads a table of at most a few thousand rows', 20261116_002) does not hold.
findings.evidence: tests/test_c2_ops_recheck.py::test_a_burst_of_sign_ins_with_made_up_logins_does_not_hold_the_signed_in_users_requests holds _scrypt on an Event, sends threads+2 sign-ins with made-up logins, and waits until every executor thread is inside a password check. A signed-in user's GET /api/v1/auth/session then gets no answer within 3 s (fails: answer None). Control, run in a scratch file and removed: the same test with a 64-thread default executor passes, so the wait is executor exhaustion. auth_throttle growth, measured on my cluster: 4M rows (one per typed login) = 1053 MB. The hourly purge of 2M rows is a Seq Scan (the PK (scope, key_hash, window_start) cannot serve window_start), 1.7 s, 61539 buffers read, 30654 written. The hot per-login read stays an Index Scan on auth_throttle_pkey, 0.04 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone reaching the public origin (the Railway domain is reachable today with the switch off) sends sign-ins with random logins, as fast as scrypt allows: 1 per try now, 4 per try after the switch. All default-executor threads sit in scrypt. Every other request's to_thread database call (session resolve, Terminal gateway, Monitor, saving) queues behind them, so pages stall or time out for every signed-in user, and edge-bff memory jumps by about 16 MiB per running derivation (up to 512 MiB). The flood also writes about 260 B of auth_throttle per try, roughly 0.45 GB per day per vCPU of attack, kept 2 days and fully read by the hourly purge. Once the purge passes 5 s, finding 1 stops the AI queue.
findings.general_class: CPU-heavy work reachable without a session and without a per-client or global bound, run on the shared default executor next to all database I/O. Every unauthenticated route that hashes a password or derives a key is in the class: sign-in, register (password_verifier plus the Pwned range call, a sync httpx with a 2 s timeout, also on to_thread), password/reset, verify; later Google sign-in (Phase 1 later), Phase 5 hooks, 3e examples. Throttle tables keyed by caller-chosen text, sized by assumption, are part of the same class.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c's Terminal routes need a session and add no password work. They do share the stalled executor during a flood, but 3c does not build on the defect.
findings.affects_beta_live: Two services have two executors, so a flood on one domain does not stall the other's threads. Both still share auth_throttle and Postgres, so growth and purge load add up, and a flood on the beta address hits the live site's database.
findings.fix: Run password derivations on a small dedicated executor, or behind a semaphore of a few slots, with a queue limit that answers 429 or 503 when full, so database calls never wait behind them. Enforce a per-client bound once the Railway client-address probe (CONTRACT section 4) is done, plus a global cap on failed sign-ins per minute in the meantime. Size and purge auth_throttle for unauthenticated input: a window_start index or a batch purge in its own transaction (finding 1), and correct the migration's sizing claim.
findings.related_r1: R1-9 and R1-16 (limits keyed by a public identifier, no per-account cap) deal with lock-out and guessing. Their fixes, a proof-based way out and a per-account cap, do not bound password derivations per client, so they leave the executor exhaustion and the table growth in place.
findings.confirm_check: Run the test (about 4 s). Rerun it alone on a busy machine; a slow machine can only make it pass falsely, never fail falsely, because it waits until every thread is held.

findings.title: The Monitor shows a plan refusal as its internal code ('CAPABILITY_REQUIRED', 'MFA_REQUIRED') instead of its words, and every non-admin account lands on it after sign-in or registration
findings.root_cause: edge-client.js api() builds ApiError with message = the code (data.error.code) and puts the refusal's words only on error.text (static/edge-client.js:47-48). The Monitor ignores error.text and renders setApiError(e.message) in its alert (static/index.html:12078, 12081, 12135, 12147 conversation load, 12169 submit; rendered at :12299 as div.auth-error[role=alert]). The sign-out path does the same with notify(e.message) (:11497, :11515). M471 (Phase 0) records that the shell shows a plan refusal's words; the Monitor never does.
findings.evidence: Browser run, switch on (tests/test_c2_e2e_people.py::test_the_monitor_shows_a_plan_refusal_in_words_not_its_code, commit 98ac31f3). A free account registered through /register and the emailed code lands on the Monitor. GET /api/v1/conversations answers 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED with message 'This feature is not part of your EDGE plan. Upgrade the plan to use it; you are still signed in.'. The page alert reads exactly 'CAPABILITY_REQUIRED' (AssertionError: assert 'CAPABILITY_REQUIRED' != 'CAPABILITY_REQUIRED'). A paid account shows the same, because decision D1 gives the paid plan monitor.example and not monitor.view. In a second run, after the plan was raised to one needing the second factor, the alert read 'MFA_REQUIRED'. p3c-int 41067e7d does not touch static/ or shared/ (git diff --stat bf273f52 41067e7d), so the defect is the same there.
findings.failure_scenario: EDGE_MULTIUSER on: a person registers, enters the code and is signed in directly. The first screen is the Monitor, with a red alert 'CAPABILITY_REQUIRED' and a working composer. Sending a question gives the same code. The admin meets the same for other refusals: 'MFA_REQUIRED' when a session needs the second factor, LIMIT_REACHED when the deferred daily cap of D1 lands, and PLAN_EXPIRED if the admin plan lapses.
findings.general_class: A shell component that shows ApiError.message (the code) instead of error.text (the words). The shared module and the six Vite pages word refusals through accessText; the Monitor's nine setApiError(e.message) sites, the side-chat frame (the same component at /c/<id>?view=side) and the sign-out notify do not. Gates (d) is broken at the first screen of every new account. 3e plans an example conversation for plans without monitor.view, but its list does not mention the shell's alert. The alert stays for every refusal the admin can meet, and for any later Monitor plan (D1's ledger and daily cap, Phase 5 PLAN_EXPIRED).
findings.affects_3c_why: Front-end of the shell only. 3c changes no shell code and does not depend on it.
findings.affects_beta_live: No difference with two edge-bff versions on one database. Each site serves its own shell, and the defect shows on whichever version has not fixed it.
findings.fix: In the Monitor (and the sign-out notify), show e.text || e.message, so refusals in the error contract show their words. Alternatively let edge-client.js put the words into the ApiError message for access refusals. Add the Monitor alert to the M471 front-end contract test, and have 3e list that a plan without monitor.view never lands on a refused Monitor.

findings.title: The shell never re-reads its own session when X-Edge-Entitlements changes: an account raised to a plan that needs the second factor is stuck in the workspace (no way to /mfa) until a reload
findings.root_cause: The shell keeps two copies of the session. One is window.Edge's `auth` (static/edge-client.js:185-193); it is set only by Edge.session(), signin, adopt and the 'cleared' hook (:17). The other is the shared module's `edge` client. Only the module reads X-Edge-Entitlements (shared/edge-session.ts:427-432 noteVersion) and handles the 'entitlements' broadcast (:414), and that only invalidates the module's own client. edge-client.js api() (:25-27) never reads the header, and no hook re-reads `auth` on a version change. The shell decides its routing from that stale copy: authMode reads Edge.auth.access.next (index.html:13666-13668), and MfaPage reads access.mfa_enrolled (:11821). CONTRACT 8a and 12 say the version header makes the session be re-read.
findings.evidence: Browser run, switch on (tests/test_c2_e2e_people.py::test_a_plan_raised_to_one_that_needs_mfa_asks_for_the_authenticator_without_a_reload, commit 98ac31f3). A paid account is signed in. Its subscription is moved to the plan holding '*', as Phase 4 would do. The shell then navigates to /terminal and back to /monitor. The server's session answers access.next 'mfa', mfa_enrolled false and version db-0c9a48b9c40f. The shell's Edge.auth.access still has plan 'paid' and version db-c85446158b5a (AssertionError on the version). In the exploration run the Monitor alert read 'MFA_REQUIRED'. The Screener frame said 'This needs your sign-in code. Enter the code from your authenticator app, then try again.', although the account has no authenticator. Navigating to /mfa still showed the workspace. Only page.reload() showed 'Set up your authenticator'. Route answers carry no mfa_enrolled (principal.py:244 raise Refusal(403, 'MFA_REQUIRED')).
findings.failure_scenario: Phase 4: the admin raises a signed-in user to the admin plan, or gives an override of admin.access. On that person's next click every route answers 403 MFA_REQUIRED. The shell keeps the workspace, the pages tell them to enter a code from an authenticator they never set up, and /mfa does not open. Nothing says to reload. Any plan change reaches the shell's copy only at a reload, a sign-in or another tab's 'cleared'.
findings.general_class: A second, unversioned copy of an entitlement-bearing object held beside the versioned one. Every decision the shell takes from Edge.auth.access goes stale on a plan change, a lowering (D5), an expiry or an override. Today that covers the MFA routing and enrolment start. 3e will add the rail's example mode per <tab>.view, lock prompts, the upgrade prompt and the expired-plan words, all from the same copy, so a lowered plan would keep loading real tabs and a raised one would keep the examples until a reload. The same applies to the Phase 4 admin page and the Phase 5 /pay flow. The shell's models list (loaded once per session) has the same shape.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c is server-side (edge-bff headers, terminal-api). The stale copy matters for 3e and Phase 4, which build on the shell's access object.
findings.affects_beta_live: Worse with two edge-bff versions on one database. A plan change made through one site (the Phase 4 page on the beta) reaches sessions on the other site on their next request, and the other site's shell, whichever version it runs, keeps its stale copy too.
findings.fix: Have edge-client.js api() read X-Edge-Entitlements; on a change, re-read /api/v1/auth/session into `auth` and dispatch 'edge-auth'. Alternatively subscribe the shell to the module's version change (a hook beside onCleared for 'entitlements', and for this tab's own noteVersion). Give the MFA_REQUIRED refusal details.mfa_enrolled on every route (as the sign-in does), so the words and the page can offer the set-up. Test: a plan change while signed in reaches the shell's access with no reload.

findings.title: Under Phase 3c the free plan's Terminal draws nothing, not even BBCA: p3c-int refuses every reference file (D3), and the Terminal page cannot draw without the ticker list
findings.root_cause: The Terminal page's liveData (terminal/src/data/live.ts:270 tickersP = reference('tickers'); :306 const tickers = await tickersP) awaits the ticker reference list before it draws anything. A refusal rejects liveData, and the page shows only the refusal. On p3c-int, terminal_access.check answers `elif head == 'reference': _dataset(caps, REFERENCE)` for every non-admin. For the free plan (8a seed: terminal.dataset {ids:[price]}, terminal.tickers [BBCA]; D3 = B 'tanpa daftar ticker') that means 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED terminal.dataset:reference for tickers, brokers, logos and fixed_income. CONTRACT 8b lets /reference 'refuse or filter'; p3c-int refuses, and 3c defers the page side to 3e. 3e's Terminal list ('picks an allowed ticker', 'search marks locked tickers') assumes the page has a ticker list; it neither says the page must draw without one nor resolves the contradiction with D3.
