findings.title: Two edge-bff services on one database act on shared rows with their own switch, configuration and code: the queue loop that claims a job judges it by its own rules, and a switch-off start rewrites user #1's password identity
findings.root_cause: Phases 0-3b assume one edge-bff per database. (1) BacktestStore.claim (backtest.py:650-660) and the Monitor worker take the oldest queued row with no site filter; the dispatch re-check resolves the owner through the claiming service's own Auth.owner_principal (backtest.py:766, :933-944; worker.py:79-92), which with EDGE_MULTIUSER off is switch_off_principal (principal.py:184-196, :347-351): an owner EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS does not list holds nothing. (2) AccountStore.seed copies the starting service's EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER over user #1's password identity whenever that service has the switch off (accounts.py:121-124), although a switch-on service treats that identity as the account's own (password change and reset, auth_flows.py _set_password). (3) The Phase 3b allow.FAMILIES reads backtest.indicator, backtest.flow_indicator, screener.indicator and screener.flow_indicator (allow.py:65-70), rows the 3c follow-up migration deletes (p3c-int 20261118_001 lines 34-39); its own rollback comment already says the older edge-bff needs these rows.
findings.evidence: Tests in verification/edge_multiuser/access_tiers/pending/test_r2_trace_beta_live.py (commit b84efe4c), run from apps/edge-bff/tests on my cluster: (a) a paid account's backtest submitted to the switch-on app and claimed by run_next on a switch-off app on the same database ends state FAILED, error {code: CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, capability: backtest.run}, and the worker is never called (assert at line 47). (b) The switch-on app starts, user #1's identity verifier is replaced (as a change on that site does), the switch-off app starts: the identity holds the switch-off service's env verifier again (assert at line 63). (c) Probe (not committed): with the Phase 3b allow.py, a paid principal's allow was indicator 53 / flow_indicator 54 ids for both workers before p3c-int 20261118_001 and 0 / 0 after it (candle_pattern 20 and screener_metric 55 unchanged).
findings.failure_scenario: Beta site with EDGE_MULTIUSER on, live site off, one database, both with EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED: a paid user queues a backtest on beta; if the live loop claims it first the job ends FAILED 'not part of your EDGE plan'. A second admin account (u_ owner with '*') queues a Monitor run on beta; the live loop refuses it at dispatch. The admin changes or resets user #1's password on beta; the next live deploy silently restores the env password. Once both sites have the switch on and beta applies the 3c follow-up migration while live still runs the 3b code, every paid user on live loses all indicator and Flow items in the Backtest and Screener (CAPABILITY_REQUIRED on any run with an indicator).
findings.general_class: Per-service configuration and code applied to rows every service shares. Other routes and tables in the class: edge_bff.jobs (Monitor dispatch, worker.py refused), edge_bff.backtest_jobs (dispatch and the allow expanded from the claiming service's releases.json), the seed and seed subscription at start, user #1's sessions (a live switch-off site reads any session row of EDGE_OWNER, store.session, including a beta session still pending MFA, and gives '*' with no MFA, so beta's admin MFA is bypassable by signing in on the switch-off site with the same password the seed copied), beta's sign-out-all and reset revoke only user_id sessions, not the switch-off site's. Later: 3c deploy step 4 ('terminal-api requires the headers') refuses every Terminal call of an edge-bff version older than 3c; any catalog migration that deletes or renames rows an older edge-bff reads (Phase 4 admin plans, Phase 5 payment states) needs expand-then-contract ordering.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c's own migration 20261118_001 removes rows the deployed 3b code reads (probe: paid allow 53/54 to 0/0), and 3c deploy step 4 would break an older edge-bff that sends no owner headers. With a single edge-bff and the switch off nothing changes today; with two versions on one database both need an ordering rule.
findings.affects_beta_live: Appears only with two edge-bff services on one database (not built). Every part above needs the two-site design to decide: one queue loop per site with a site column on edge_bff.jobs and backtest_jobs (or one switch state for both sites), a seed that never copies the env verifier while another site runs with the switch on, MFA for user #1 on every site, and migrations that keep the previous edge-bff version working until it is replaced.
findings.confirm_check: Copy pending/test_r2_trace_beta_live.py into apps/edge-bff/tests and run it with EDGE_TEST_POSTGRES_URL: both tests fail at lines 47 and 63.
findings.fix: Decide in the two-site design, then make the pending tests pass in apps/edge-bff/tests: tag queued rows with the site that made them and claim only one's own (or run the loops on one site only, with one switch state); have AccountStore.seed copy the verifier only when no switch-on site exists (or never once the switch was on); run migrations that remove catalog rows only after no running edge-bff reads them (keep the four families until both sites run the 3b follow-up); hold 3c deploy step 4 until every edge-bff sends the headers.

findings.title: Plan saved-item caps answer 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED while the backtest queue cap answers 429 LIMIT_REACHED: two codes for one contract concept, and the shared module treats only one as a plan refusal
findings.root_cause: CONTRACT section 3 gives plan limits one code, 429 LIMIT_REACHED (details.limit, retry_after_s), whose front-end reaction is the limit message. Phase 3a made terminal.layouts_max, terminal.presets_max, terminal.drawings_max, screener.saved_items and watchlist.lists/per_list/indicators plan limits but kept their old refusal 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED with details.limit = the local name ('layouts', 'presets', 'sets', 'saved_items', 'lists', 'tickers', 'indicators') and a message that only says to delete one (layouts.py:154-157, presets.py:128-130, drawings.py:121, screener.py:510, watchlist.py:94-95). M481 C3 F1/C1 F2 changed only backtest.queued_jobs to LIMIT_REACHED, giving as the reason 'the contract's code for a plan limit' (backtest.py:1405-1412). Nothing recorded why the other plan caps differ. The shared module maps only LIMIT_REACHED to kind 'limit' (edge-session.ts:301-303), so isAccessRefusal (:336) and accessText (:349) never fire for LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
findings.evidence: The existing tests lock both codes: tests/test_phase3a_gates.py:266-269 asserts 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED with details {limit: 'layouts'|'presets'|'sets'|'saved_items'|'watchlist'|'lists'|'tickers'|'indicators'} for the plan caps lowered by override; :330 asserts 429 LIMIT_REACHED for backtest.queued_jobs, with the comment 'C1 F2: a plan limit'. ERRORS M481 row C3 F1, C1 F2.
findings.failure_scenario: Switch on, an account whose plan or override sets terminal.layouts_max below what it wants: saving a layout answers 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED 'At most N layouts: delete one before saving another.' The shared module classes it as 'other' (no upgrade sentence, no plan refusal), details.limit does not name the capability, so a 3e lock prompt keyed on the plan refusal never shows for these caps, while the queue cap shows 'reached your plan's limit ... or upgrade the plan'.
findings.general_class: One contract concept answered with different codes by different routes, so a client rule keyed by code covers only some of them. Same check for 3c's quota refusals (LIMIT_REACHED 429, consistent with the queue cap), Phase 4 admin limits and Phase 5 payment limits. Note that a 429 must carry Retry-After (CONTRACT 3), which fits a quota or queue but not a cap where waiting does not help; the contract needs one sentence for caps.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c's Terminal quota refusals use 429 LIMIT_REACHED like the queue cap; 3c adds no saved-item cap. The gap reaches 3e (lock and upgrade prompts read the shared module's kinds).

findings.title: Contract requirements whose code no test holds: removing the code leaves every suite green (session absolute lifetime in both modes, the MFA 429 Retry-After, the default no-store, display-name loading, and others)
findings.root_cause: Each requirement below was tested only through a neighbour (the idle timeout, the code-try Retry-After, the need() refusal path), so a regression of the requirement itself passes.
findings.evidence: Mutation runs on my cluster (r2_trace, port 55537), base suite 657 passed / 1 skipped without the round-1 files. SURVIVED (tests still green): (1) store.py:90 drop 'AND expires_at>now()': switch-off sessions never expire (CONTRACT 2 and 4: absolute lifetime 24 h); 73 passed. (2) accounts.py:140 drop 's.expires_at > now()': switch-on sessions never expire while used within the idle window; 82 passed. (3) auth_flows.py:552 drop the Retry-After header of 429 LIMIT_REACHED mfa_tries (CONTRACT 3 'Retry-After on every 429'); 59 passed. (4) main.py:647 drop request.state.principal on the sign-in answer: no X-Edge-Entitlements on it (CONTRACT 8a 'every answer made for a principal'); 98 passed. By reading, register/verify (auth_flows.py:466-482) never sets request.state.principal, so its signed-in answer carries no header at all. (5) main.py:261 drop the start-up display-name load, or principal.py:321 drop the refresh on a need() refusal: each alone 54 and 50 passed. Refusals outside auth.need (BacktestLoop.dispatch principal.refusal, worker.refused, run_refusal/model_refusal, admin() refusal(admin.access), allow.named relays, and p3c-int terminal_access.check -> capability_required) get names only from the start-up load, which nothing tests. (6) main.py:364 drop the default Cache-Control: no-store: 138 passed across test_edge, test_error_contract, test_principal, test_terminal, test_backtest; it is what keeps per-user JSON (preferences, lists, catalog, /api/terminal/v1 relays) out of a shared browser's HTTP cache (CONTRACT 13.8). (7) accounts.py:44 drop 's.starts_at <= now()': 80 passed. (8) auth_flows.py:139 stop recording SEND_IP (CONTRACT 4: recorded until the probe): 65 passed. (9) principal.py:55 remove sign-out from MFA_OPEN: 97 passed. (10) The plain-words rule (test_error_contract.py:26-28) covers only errors.MESSAGES; applied to the other message tables it finds pages.py:43-44 NOT_CONFIGURED naming EDGE_TERMINAL_URL and TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY, a message the Radar, Overview and Watchlist pages show (radar/src/api.ts:25). KILLED (held): entitlements on refusals, page-file no-cache on 200 and 304, disabled account, models default hidden, seed flag, resend payload nulled, svix tolerance, pwned timeout, code email expiry, TOTP window, pending session limited to MFA_OPEN, admin() MFA, registration cookie deleted, reset revokes, change notifies.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit drops 'expires_at>now()' from store.session (switch-off, the path deployed on dev now) or from accounts.resolve: a session token used at least every 8 hours stays valid for ever, and CI stays green. A refactor removes the default no-store: per-user answers become cacheable and user B on A's browser can be served A's preferences or lists from the HTTP cache, and CI stays green.
findings.general_class: A requirement locked only through a neighbouring requirement. The same applies to 3c's new answers (the cut relay's Cache-Control private, the quota 429's Retry-After) and to every later 429 and every later refusal outside auth.need: a route-derived or AST test (every Refusal(429, ...) passes a Retry-After header; every handler that builds a refusal names a display name from the loaded catalog) would cover them by construction.
findings.affects_3c_why: 3c's terminal refusals (terminal_access.check) take their display names only from the start-up load (item 5), and 3c's cut and relay answers rely on the default no-store for their error answers (item 6); neither is tested.
findings.affects_beta_live: Item 5 gets worse with two services: a catalog migration applied for one service adds capability rows the other service names only after a need() refusal refreshes them (or a restart).
findings.confirm_check: Apply each mutation listed in the evidence to ae9a1d8f and run the named test files (or the whole edge-bff suite): each stays green.
findings.related_r1: R1-28 (the SSE re-check, same class) and R1-46 (database backstops); the sites above are not in either
findings.fix: Add tests that fail on each mutation: an expired session (UPDATE edge_bff.sessions SET expires_at = now() - interval '1 second') answers 401 in both modes; the MFA 429 carries Retry-After; the sign-in and register/verify answers carry X-Edge-Entitlements (and set request.state.principal in register_verify); a dispatch refusal's details.display_name is the catalog's name with the need() refresh removed; every /api answer without its own Cache-Control is no-store; a future-starting subscription resolves to the default plan; a send records SEND_IP; a pending session can sign out; the plain-words rule runs over every message table (and the NOT_CONFIGURED text loses the variable names).

Every switch-off start also copies the env verifier onto user #1's identity (accounts.py:121-124), so the password a phisher holds for the switch-on site normally opens the switch-off sign-in directly, with no carried cookie needed. Idle sessions and status are not checked for switch-off sessions either, by design. The exposure the fix removes is narrow: the identity's password differs from EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER (env rotated during an incident while the attacker holds a pending cookie), or EDGE_LOGIN is unknown to the attacker (the seed username is admin_1 when EDGE_LOGIN is reserved). Under the agreed architecture the beta is 'admin only, registration refused', which presumes accounts (switch on) on the beta too, so no switch-off site on the shared database is planned. What remains is the switch's way back and a pre-Phase-1 rollback, and the fix cannot cover the latter. The one-line fix is still worth doing. The real constraint to record for Phase 6 and the beta/live plan: a switch-off build on a database that holds switch-on accounts bypasses MFA for user #1. verdicts.reason: Confirmed. lifespan reads store.ready once and gates the AI worker, the email sender and (inside the worker) every purge on that one read. /ready re-reads on each healthcheck, so Railway marks the deployment SUCCESS and keeps it. With the switch on, this latch is the only start of the email sender, so a boot during any database error stops every registration and reset code silently until the next deploy. verdicts.reason: Confirmed, with no other layer. Reset and change write the identity and revoke sessions without any lock the sign-in or change path waits on. The change's verifier UPDATE is unconditional, and it never re-checks that its own session is still live. The sign-in inserts its session after a slow proof, with no compare against the current verifier. A later resolve checks revoked_at, but the session was created after the revoke, so it passes. Account recovery is the guarantee that a reset evicts a holder of the old password or session (CONTRACT :114 and :154), and with a looping attacker the race defeats it most of the time: the change window includes the Pwned range call (up to 2 s). A session-holder looping changes can keep the owner out (see R2-10 for the second half of that lock-out). Severity stays blocks-switch-on.

Code: auth_flows.py:290-292 (UPDATE identities ... WHERE user_id only); :300-307 (change: no liveness check of keep_token_hash); :505-519 (verify, then new_verifier with the Pwned call, then store.change); :269-287 (reset locks register:<email> and users FOR UPDATE, not the identity or the sessions:<id> lock); main.py:604-641 (find_login, 4 derivations, create_session); accounts.py:219-232 (only sessions:<id> lock). p3c-int leaves auth_flows.py, accounts.py and main.py's sign-in unchanged.

The same lock must be taken by sign-out-all (accounts.revoke_all) and by mfa/verify (revoke the pending session first, then create the new one only if a row was revoked), else those sites keep the same race.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. _may_send refuses any code email while any outbox row to the address is younger than 60 s, whatever its purpose. password_changed and account_exists are such rows, and the forgot route answers 202 CODE_SENT either way. password_changed is enqueued with enqueue(), not _send(), so it is not even counted in SEND_EMAIL: a session-holder who knows the password they set can change it every <60 s without limit (a success clears change:<id>). Every forgot of the owner is then silently not mailed, so self-service recovery is gone indefinitely. Together with R2-9 this is a persistent takeover, so blocks-switch-on is right. verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The cap decision, the code check and the count run in separate transactions with no account lock, so concurrent tries all pass the read. The gain is bounded by MFA_USER (10 per 15 min, decided atomically under an advisory lock): at most 9 extra TOTP checks per cap crossing, and up to 10 recovery checks instead of 2 per 24 h lock (LOCK_SECONDS 86400). That is negligible against a 6-digit TOTP with a ±1 step window and 10-character base32 recovery codes. Still, the documented NIST guarantee does not hold under concurrency.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and the trigger is more realistic than the finder's large-table setup suggests. Each pending registration carries its own email_codes row (register then _issue_code). Without an index on email_codes(user_id), the purge's ON DELETE CASCADE scans all of email_codes once per deleted account, so the purge's work grows with the square of the pending backlog. A few thousand never-verified registrations in a day pass the 5 s statement_timeout with no other data. Register needs no session, and SEND_IP is not enforced. Once it fails it never recovers, because the backlog only grows. The worker then retries every poll and never reaches the claim, the other purges roll back with it, and a 5 s failing DELETE runs about every 7 s on the shared Postgres (one vCPU, also used by the data jobs). No other layer bounds it. The same coupling is in BacktestLoop.run (prune and reap before claim in one try).

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Every scrypt runs through asyncio.to_thread on the loop's default executor, the same pool every database call uses (session resolve included); nothing in app/ sets another executor. Nothing bounds derivations per client or overall, because SIGNIN_IP is recorded only and a made-up login each try never meets SIGNIN_LOGIN. A flood of made-up logins therefore stalls every signed-in user's requests and inserts throttle rows without bound. One correction to 'Since Phase 0': the pre-Phase-0 limiter checked len(attempts) before the scrypt but appended only after it, so a concurrent burst passed it too. It bounded only sustained floods, at about 5 failures a minute per proxy address. Phase 0 removed that sustained bound, and Phase 1 multiplied the derivations per try by 4. The public dev site is exposed today with the switch off.

Dockerfile:97 (--workers 1, no concurrency limit). 98be0931^ main.py:512-524 (old limiter: check before, append after the derivation).
verdicts.better_root_cause: CPU-heavy unauthenticated work on the executor shared with all database I/O, with no per-client or global admission bound. The pre-Phase-0 limiter was not a concurrency bound either, so the burst exhaustion is older than Phase 0; the sustained-flood exposure is Phase 0's.
verdicts.fix_assessment: A small dedicated executor or semaphore for derivations, with a queue limit that answers 429/503, covers sign-in. The same must wrap register, reset and password change (new_verifier plus the Pwned call on to_thread). A global failed-sign-in cap until the client-address probe is done, plus a window_start index or batched purge for auth_throttle, cover the growth.
